notes:
1. Title says "banks plan for fewer desks" and the dek/title frame it as a trend. Source: only Barclays announced cuts ("British lender Barclays has revealed plans to cut 5,000 jobs"), and the cuts are in "support functions, including developers", not desks. Fix: name Barclays or make it singular, e.g. "Agents get spending limits while Barclays plans fewer support roles" (under 70 characters).
2. Dek says "Walmart gave shoppers spending caps for agents" and heading 2 says "Walmart caps what agents can spend". Source (TechCrunch): "With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to ... authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set." The controls are not live yet. Fix: "Walmart is giving shoppers spending caps for agents" and a heading such as "Walmart plans spending caps for agents".
3. Section 2 opens "Meanwhile Walmart launched". Walmart announced "on Wednesday" (21 Oct), Barclays reported "Thursday" (22 Oct), so the stories are not simultaneous. Fix: drop "Meanwhile" or write "A day earlier, Walmart launched ...".
4. Section 3 opens "At the same time, a report on Wednesday ... said the hackers used". "the hackers" has no antecedent in the note, and "At the same time" links it to Barclays (Thursday). Source: "A hacking group known as CyberCartel reportedly used ... That's according to a report Wednesday (Oct. 21) from The Information". Fix: "A report on Wednesday from The Information said a hacking group known as CyberCartel used a web of AI agents ...".
5. Section 1 says the earnings presentation "described" the quote. Source: "the earnings presentation, which also noted an outcome was 'organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.'" Fix: "noted an outcome was".
6. Brief 2026-10-22-walmart-agent-gateway-spending-controls, note field says "The design mirrors an authorized user on a credit card, a structure card issuers already know how to cap and track." Source: "The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending." The brief states Walmart's comparison as fact and adds an unsourced claim about card issuers. Fix: "Walmart says the controls are similar to adding an authorized user on a credit card, where transactions are identified and spending can be capped." (the email card repeats this line.)
